key_insight: Reported gains in Multimodal Domain Generalization often reflect inconsistent evaluation protocols and narrow benchmarks rather than true algorithmic progress; a unified, comprehensive benchmark reveals which methods genuinely generalize across modalities and domains.
problem_solved: Addresses the fragmentation and evaluation variability in MMDG research by providing a standardized, broad benchmark that tests algorithms across diverse datasets, modality configurations, and real-world settings beyond action recognition.
method: Assemble a diverse benchmark suite spanning multiple tasks and modality combinations (not just action recognition) to capture real-world domain shifts.
Define and enforce standardized evaluation protocols (training/validation/test splits, pre-processing, and metrics) to eliminate protocol-induced performance artifacts.
Systematically evaluate representative MMDG algorithms, run ablations to attribute gains, and produce best-practice recommendations for fair comparison and deployment.
impact: Enables fair, reproducible comparison of multimodal generalization methods and helps practitioners identify approaches that truly improve robustness across domains—accelerating trustworthy deployment of multimodal systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing benchmark construction: datasets → standardized protocol → algorithm evaluation → analysis
Grouped bar chart comparing algorithm performance across multiple datasets/modalities to highlight inconsistent gains
Heatmap or matrix showing how evaluation choices (preprocessing, splits, metrics) alter reported results
Checklist/roadmap infographic with recommended best practices for MMDG evaluation and dataset selection
paper_title: Are We Making Progress in Multimodal Domain Generalization? A Comprehensive Benchmark Study
paper_authors: Hao Dong, Hongzhao Li, Shupan Li, Muhammad Haris Khan, Eleni Chatzi
